quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 40 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: Where is the gearshift located?
questions.correctAnswerText: By the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: What should you do when riding in the rain?

options.text: Ride down the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in tire tracks left by other cars.
questions.explanation: Roads are slippery when rain first starts to fall. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. This gives you better grip on the road.

questions.question: What should happen when you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle?

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to signal that the other vehicle should proceed.
You should continue through the intersection and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply steady pressure to both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: What should you do after riding over an object on the road?

options.text: Continue riding because the danger has passed.
Pull to the side of the road and check your tires and rims for damage.
Stop to remove the object from the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and check your tires and rims for damage.
questions.explanation: After riding over an object, pull off the road and check your tires and rims for damage. Also check that nothing is stuck in the drive chain or belt before you ride again.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Allow you to blend in with traffic.
Encourage others to use your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide an escape route.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should keep you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards. It should prevent other drivers from sharing your lane and give you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: What is true about reflective and brightly-colored helmets and clothing?

options.text: They should only be worn when riding at night.
They can help motorcycle riders be more visible.
They do not increase a motorcycle rider's safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can help motorcycle riders be more visible.
questions.explanation: Wearing brightly-colored or reflective clothing increases your chances of being seen by other drivers.

questions.question: What helps reduce the chance of a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Using proper lane positions.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible, signal your intentions, keep safe space around you, look at least 12 seconds ahead, identify hazards, and be ready to react to changes.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
Drivers may proceed through the intersection with caution.
Drivers must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop and wait for a signal that allows you to turn in your direction.

questions.question: How do you become sober after drinking alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: The only way to sober up is to give your body time to remove the alcohol. Nothing else speeds up this process.

questions.question: When choosing a jacket for protection, it should:

options.text: Fit loosely and flap in the wind.
Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
Not be made of leather or sturdy material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Choose a jacket made of leather or other sturdy material. It should fit snugly enough to not flap in the wind, but loose enough to let you move freely.

questions.question: When riding behind another vehicle at night, how can you tell if there are bumps ahead?

options.text: Listen for the other vehicle scraping the pavement.
Watch the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.
Look at the rear bumper and see if it bounces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the other vehicle's taillights bounce up and down.
questions.explanation: Watch the vehicle ahead of you to see road conditions at night. If the taillights bounce up and down, there are bumps on the road ahead.

questions.question: An ideal lane position should:

options.text: Help you see and be seen better.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Allow other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see and be seen better.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and lets them see you. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you a way to escape danger.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance if:
questions.correctAnswerText: It is raining.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when it takes longer to stop, when you can't see through the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy and other drivers might cut in front of you.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, make sure it:
questions.correctAnswerText: Has no cracks or defects.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state safety standards. It should fit snugly all around and have no visible damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because:

options.text: The front tire controls steering, which affects your balance.
A flat front tire disables the front brake.
A flat front tire prevents you from accelerating.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front tire controls steering, which affects your balance.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it affects steering, which is needed to maintain balance. Heavy steering feel may indicate a flat front tire.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcycle takes:

options.text: Less time to stop and speed up than usual.
The same time to stop and speed up as usual.
More time to stop and speed up than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: More time to stop and speed up than usual.
questions.explanation: Extra weight makes a motorcycle slower to accelerate and decelerate. Your motorcycle will respond more slowly when carrying a passenger than when you ride alone.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: To reduce fatigue while riding, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Take frequent rest breaks.
questions.explanation: Take frequent rest breaks on long rides to reduce fatigue. Caffeine may make fatigue worse once it wears off. Wind, rain, and cold can increase fatigue, so dress warmly and use a windshield on long trips.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Speed up to cross the surface faster.
Exaggerate the zigzag to get other drivers' attention.
Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: When your motorcycle weaves on grooves or gratings, keep a steady speed and go straight across. Trying to correct the weave by angling creates more dangerous zigzagging.

questions.question: When cars merge from an entrance ramp, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: Assume the entering drivers can see you.
Never assume the entering drivers can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume the entering drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Give merging cars plenty of space. Never assume drivers see you. Change lanes away from the entering traffic if you can. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to let them merge safely.

questions.question: What should you do if you must ride on a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed. Avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes gently when braking.

questions.question: Wearing what gives you the best chance of surviving a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: A DOT-compliant helmet.
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets Department of Transportation (DOT) standards gives you the best head and neck protection. Wearing a good-quality, properly secured helmet is the single most effective way to survive a crash.

questions.question: Wearing what helps you avoid serious facial injury in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Face or eye protection.
questions.explanation: A helmet is your best defense against injury. A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your face from injury in a crash.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden movements.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, sudden changes in speed or direction can cause a skid. Accelerate, shift gears, turn, and brake as smoothly as possible.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect your riding ability?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can hurt your ability to safely ride. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet during a crash is:

options.text: Less likely to survive than someone without a helmet.
Just as likely to survive as someone without a helmet.
More likely to survive than someone without a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: More likely to survive than someone without a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries than riders wearing helmets during a crash, regardless of speed.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash?

options.text: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.
questions.explanation: Wearing a high-quality, securely fastened helmet is the most important thing you can do to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: What should proper eye protection do?

options.text: Is not needed if your motorcycle has a windshield.
Is only needed in bad weather.
Allow you to see clearly to both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow you to see clearly to both sides.
questions.explanation: California law requires proper face and eye protection. A face shield protects your face during a collision. Good eye or face protection must let you see clearly to both sides.

questions.question: How can you help other drivers see your motorcycle?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your headlight.
questions.explanation: Using your headlight is the best way to help other drivers see your motorcycle. Always check that your headlight works before you ride.

questions.question: Why is it helpful to keep space between you and other vehicles?

options.text: You can draft off other vehicles more easily.
You have more time to react to what other drivers do.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: Keep space around your motorcycle at all times. If a problem appears, you will have time to respond and room to move safely.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle rider do to avoid crashes?

options.text: Keep enough space between you and other vehicles.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep enough space between you and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Keep a safe distance between your motorcycle and other vehicles. Maintain this space when following, being followed, passing, being passed, or sharing a lane.

questions.question: Which material gives the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather or strong synthetic materials offer the most protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign (white with red and black markings). It tells drivers what traffic laws apply in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What should you NOT check before riding your motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Inspect your paint.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, controls, lights, signals, mirrors, brakes, oil, fluids, chassis, and stands.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A stop sign is coming ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is coming ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should:

options.text: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
Assume the driver already sees you.
Ride on the far left side of the lane.
Ride on the far right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position yourself so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. This is where drivers are most likely to notice you.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding during the day?

options.text: Bright-colored clothes so other drivers can see you better.
Any color clothing since drivers can see you in daylight.
Dark-colored clothing to stand out against sunlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright-colored clothes so other drivers can see you better.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Always wear bright colors to be more visible, even during the day.

questions.question: When should you inspect your motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. It only takes a few minutes and helps prevent problems before you ride.

questions.question: What is most important about your helmet to get the best protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: It fits snugly.
questions.explanation: Your helmet gives you the best protection when it meets DOT and state standards, fits snugly all the way around, and has no damage.
